A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-CriTeach research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A.1–A.9 support reliable comparison after matching reformatted and redisplayed content.

before.justification: v2 reports original planning benchmarks, component and Llama backbone ablations, UR5e robot experiments, and a VLA demonstration, including results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical outcomes and adds LCCS reward and SCT-Qwen3-8B results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: Domain generation, repair and pruning, symbolic-to-CoT transformation, SFT, CPO objectives, and inference remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and the appendices. LCCS is introduced as an experimental comparison variant.

E1.justification: Both retain the same Blocksworld variants, three unseen planning tasks, UR5e room and wet-lab tasks, and VLA table-organization demonstration. The added reward and backbone experiments use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds SCT-LCCS-4B, using the Longest Contiguous Common Subsequence reward attributed to Huang et al. (2025c), alongside the retained component comparisons. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 8 extends the experimental model configurations by applying full SCT training to Qwen3-8B, previously included only as a baseline. Existing splits, metrics, prompts, token limits, and reported SFT/CPO training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds an alternative partial-progress reward ablation and an SCT-Qwen3-8B backbone experiment. The Llama backbone analysis already appeared in v2 Appendix A.9; its new main-text summary does not constitute a new experiment.

E5.justification: Both retain point estimates and ten trials per real-robot task. There are no changes to seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds SCT-LCCS-4B overall success/progress of 0.31/0.71 in Table 3 and SCT-Qwen3-8B results of 0.49/0.79 in Table 4. Shared numerical results, including SCT-4B's 0.46/0.76, robot outcomes, token counts, and appendix Llama scores, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, and metric formulas remain equivalent. v3 displays the existing ground-atom set definition as a numbered equation, shifting subsequent numbering without adding mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the dual use of generated domains for supervision and rewards, together with planning, generalization, efficiency, and noisy-state robustness claims. Backbone generality was already claimed in v2 Appendix A.9; the expanded conclusion does not materially redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Section 8 more explicitly distinguishes SFT's complete-plan success from RL's partial-plan progress and interprets LCCS results. Sections 7, 9, and 10 expand explanations involving reasoning-oriented training, VLM state refinement, and applicability limits for weak backbones, deformable objects, contact-rich manipulation, and geometric reasoning.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page project website link. Implementation details, hyperparameters, prompts, pseudocode, and robot/VLA instructions remain essentially unchanged. The PDFs do not establish what code or data the linked site provides.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al. (2025c) for the LCCS comparison and Pallagani et al. (2023) for planning-related discussion, while expanding discussion of already-cited VLM refinement approaches. Graph-R1's replacement by NPG-MUSE refers to the same arXiv work and is a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract and selected results, ablation, and limitations passages, adds RQ6 and an Impact Statement, and updates affiliations and conference front matter. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reformats the main text and references into two columns, changes typography and spacing throughout, and resizes or relocates retained figures and tables. It also adds the backbone summary Table 4 and an LCCS row to Table 3; the six existing figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The LCCS comparison makes the reward analysis more informative, and the Qwen3-8B experiment adds evidence for backbone generality. Clearer SFT/RL interpretation and more concrete applicability limits improve how readers can assess the findings. These are bounded gains: the core method and most evidence, including the Llama study, were already present in v2.
